newsitem.title: GERMANY: Puma drops, tracks drop in Nike.
newsitem.headline: Puma drops, tracks drop in Nike.

text.p: Shares in German sportswear group Puma AG slumped on Monday amid what dealers said was concern the company will be hit by the weak production outlook already weighing on U.S. rival sportswear maker Nike.
Shares in Puma were down 2.30 marks ($1.35), or 3.9 percent, at 57.50 marks in late bourse trade while the 30-share DAX was flat at down 0.72 points at 3,343.79.
Nike shares have come under pressure in recent weeks in U.S. dealings after it said it was reducing production capacity.

"It's something associated with events in the U.S. where we have had sharp price declines in Nike and Reebok. I think this is spilling over currently into Germany," said Michael Wand of Paribas Capital Markets in Frankfurt on Puma's decline.
"Adidas is holding relatively well. The bashing is focusing on Puma," he added.
Adidas shares on Monday were down four marks, or 2.4 percent, at 174 marks.
"The general outlook is for a slowdown in the sporting goods industry, but I think the sell-off is overdone," Wand commented.
